matrix_to_img — 2D bridge op

• Data kinds: matrix → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "matrix_to_img", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

Usage

Turns a matrix into gray levels for viewing and back into an image — this is not a cast.

The outbound bridge (img_to_matrix) is stated explicitly to be a pure cast that changes neither values nor shape, but making the return trip a cast as well would be a lie: matrix values do not fit in [0,1], and if the minimum is simply stretched to black and the maximum to white, you cannot tell where 0 is. The signs of covariance, correlation and pseudo-inverse mean nothing unless that can be read.

• a → strength of log compression. With k = 10**(3a) - 1, y = sign(x) * log1p(k|x|) / log1p(k) (linear at a=0, 1000-fold compression at a=1). For matrices whose magnitudes spread over many orders, like condition numbers, it prevents the small entries from all collapsing to black.

• b → reference. b < 0.5 stretches the data's min–max to [0,1]; b >= 0.5 places 0 at 0.5 and scales symmetrically by the maximum of |x| (for signed matrices; 0.5 is neutral, bright = positive, dark = negative).

• Returns: float64 of the same shape as the input, range [0,1]. A matrix whose elements are all equal gives a uniform 0.5 (falls back to neutral so that the min–max side does not divide by 0 either).
